name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,300

entries.clue: Trait of tough guy moving his comma (8)

annotation.surface: A pedant notes that a tough guy writes with his comma in the wrong place.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a punctuation joke about a macho man; really only the letters of 'his comma' matter.
annotation.definitionFit: Machismo is the swaggering masculinity typical of a tough guy.

entries.clue: Pothead beginning to smoke printer’s powder (6)

indicators.note: the beginning of 'smoke' is its first letter

blocks.note: toner is the powder a laser printer uses

annotation.surface: A pothead's first puff turns out to be printer toner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Smoke' and 'powder' keep the drug scene going, but the powder is office supplies.
annotation.definitionFit: A stoner is slang for a habitual cannabis user, a pothead.

entries.clue: Fighters in the Peloponnesian War skill in bridges (8)

blocks.note: art = skill, as in 'the art of war'

annotation.surface: A remark on the engineering skill of ancient Greek soldiers.
annotation.walkthrough: The long definition reads as the subject of the sentence, which keeps the short wordplay out of sight.
annotation.definitionFit: Sparta fought Athens in the Peloponnesian War, so Spartans were fighters in it.

entries.clue: Feat of skill, the same either way (4)

indicators.note: a word that reads the same forwards and backwards is a palindrome

blocks.note: the four letters read identically from front or back

annotation.surface: A trick that works equally well whichever way you do it.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition leads to a word for feat; the rest confirms it by asking for a palindrome.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: 'deeds of valour' are feats, and 'of skill' narrows it to an impressive one.

entries.clue: Express highways for Greek island (6)

indicators.note: to express something is to say it out loud

annotation.surface: Looking for express highways on a Greek island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Express highways' reads as one phrase, like a motorway; 'Express' is a verb meaning say.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the largest of the Dodecanese, home of the ancient Colossus.

entries.clue: Man’s contribution to America (4)

indicators.note: the answer is a part contributed to the word America

annotation.surface: Praise for what one man gave to the United States.
annotation.walkthrough: Any man's name can be clued as 'man'; here the name sits inside America.
annotation.definitionFit: Eric is a man's name, so 'man' defines it by example.

entries.clue: Would like to have wife and queen, perhaps (4)

blocks.note: a queen is one kind of ant

annotation.surface: A man daydreams of having both a wife and a queen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests royalty or the Q abbreviation; the 'perhaps' shows it is an example of an ant.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: 'I would like to have a coffee' and 'I want a coffee' say the same.

entries.clue: Back of damp rathole shifted a large amount (8)

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter
letters that are shifted are rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone moved a lot of stuff out of the back of a damp rat-infested hole.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shifted a large amount' reads as a verb and its object; 'shifted' works on rathole instead.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, often in 'a plethora of options', meaning an abundance or glut.

entries.clue: Evidence of impact from sun? (6)

blocks.note: the surface suggests sunburn or a crater; the setter means the bruised eye a punch leaves
the sun gleams, so it too can be called by a word for something that gleams

annotation.surface: A question about the marks left by the sun, like sunburn.
annotation.walkthrough: Sunburn is the obvious evidence; the question mark hints that a punch leaves the evidence and the sun is only a shiner itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A shiner is slang for a black eye, the evidence of a blow.

entries.clue: Take away key electronic channel (6)

blocks.note: a duct is a channel or tube

annotation.surface: Removing an important electronic channel from a system.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like an adjective meaning important; it is a musical key.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in arithmetic and accounts: you deduct tax from pay, taking it away.

entries.clue: Drug addict sure confused (4)

annotation.surface: A drug addict who is certain and confused at once.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pairs two states of mind; 'sure' is only letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A user is slang for someone who takes illegal drugs.

entries.clue: One who kills two idiots at home (8)

annotation.surface: A killer strikes down two fools in their own house.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a crime report; the two victims are the two ASSes of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: An assassin is one who kills, especially for pay or politics.

entries.clue: Perceive object in an agitated state (8)

annotation.surface: Noticing an object that is moving about restlessly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Object' could be a verb, to protest, which fits the agitation; it is a noun, a thing.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone seething is inwardly agitated with anger.

entries.clue: Huge cold area with runny cheese in it (3,5)

indicators.note: runny cheese has lost its shape, so its letters are rearranged
the rearranged cheese goes inside IT

blocks.note: IT itself, split around the cheese

annotation.surface: A big cold room holding a stock of melting cheese.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Huge cold area' could be a fridge or warehouse; it is geography.
annotation.definitionFit: An ice sheet is a vast mass of glacial ice covering a large area.

entries.clue: Name on publication is something unimportant (8)

blocks.note: an issue of a magazine is a publication

annotation.surface: A complaint that whose name appears in print does not matter.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a dismissive remark about bylines, and 'is' joins wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A non-issue is a matter of no importance.

entries.clue: Harm popular group of twelve people? (6)

blocks.note: a jury traditionally has twelve members

annotation.surface: An accusation that a well-liked jury has done damage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Harm' could be a verb at the head of an instruction; it is the noun. The question mark marks the jury as one example of twelve people.
annotation.definitionFit: An injury is harm or damage done to someone.

entries.clue: The married people over there (4)

annotation.surface: Pointing out the married couple across the room.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The married people' looks like one phrase; the split falls after 'married'.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Them' refers to those other people, over there rather than here.

entries.clue: Jerk last to trust charming woman? (6)

blocks.note: a witch casts charms; the question mark flags the pun

annotation.surface: A cad is the last to trust a charming woman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like an insult for a man; it is a sudden movement. 'Charming' means casting spells, not pleasant.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as nouns or verbs: a sudden involuntary movement of a muscle.

entries.clue: Number ones for Nine Inch Nails, Jane’s Addiction, Suede, and The Killers? (6)

indicators.note: the number one letter of each word is its first

blocks.clueFragment: Nine Inch Nails, Jane’s Addiction, Suede
blocks.note: first letters of Nine Inch Nails Jane's Addiction Suede

annotation.surface: A question about which rock bands had number one hits.
annotation.walkthrough: The Killers look like the last band in the list; they are the definition, with the question mark showing ninjas are one kind of killer.
annotation.definitionFit: Ninjas were trained Japanese assassins, so killers.

entries.clue: Minute bit of audiotape (4)

indicators.note: the answer is a bit made of the next word's letters

annotation.surface: A sixty-second clip from a recording.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like sixty seconds of tape; it means tiny.
annotation.definitionFit: An iota is a very small amount, a minute bit.

entries.clue: Self-satisfied fool has succeeded before (4)

indicators.note: succeeded's letter is placed before the fool

blocks.note: a mug is a gullible fool

annotation.surface: A smug fool who has had success in the past.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Has succeeded before' reads as past triumph; it places S in front of MUG.
annotation.definitionFit: Smug means excessively pleased with oneself.

entries.clue: Hot number’s pinnacle (6)

blocks.note: h = hot, as on a tap

annotation.surface: A popular song reaches its peak.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hot number' reads as a hit song; the two words split into H and a number.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative synonym: 'the height of fashion' is its pinnacle, the highest point.

entries.clue: Most important performer deserts, going round bend (4,4)

indicators.note: the word goes round, so it is turned back to front

blocks.note: to rat is to desert or betray
a bend in a road is a turn

annotation.surface: The headline act walks out and drives off round a corner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deserts' looks like sandy places; it is the verb to rat on. A star turn is British for the main act on a bill.
annotation.definitionFit: A star turn is the principal act or performer in a show.

entries.clue: Gang leader abandoning prison officer (4)

indicators.note: the first letter leaves the word

blocks.note: SCREW, British slang for a prison guard, without its first letter S

annotation.surface: A gang boss walks out on a corrupt prison guard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gang leader' looks like one phrase; 'Gang' is the definition and 'leader' goes with the deletion. A screw is British slang for a prison officer.
annotation.definitionFit: A crew is a gang or group of people working together.
